newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Balloonists safe on board French boat-official.
newsitem.headline: Balloonists safe on board French boat-official.

text.p: Swiss balloonist Bertrand Piccard and Belgian Wim Verstraeten were picked up safely on Sunday by a French naval boat after ditching their Breitling Orbiter in the Mediterranean, their British flight director said.

Alan Noble told Reuters Television: "I have just spoken to the air-sea rescue and they have been picked up safely. They are now on a boat. So far as we know, they are not injured." The two were six hours into a round-the-world flight bid when they came down.

Noble said he and the team behind the flight were "obviously very, very sad" that it had to be cut short so soon after lift-off at 9 a.m. (0800 GMT) from the Swiss Alpine resort and ballooning centre of Chateau d'Oex.
"Anyone who was there will know it was such a beautiful sight. And it all went very well at first. Conditions were perfect," he said.

But some three hours into the flight, Piccard and Verstraeten reported fumes were leaking into their bright yellow gondola-cabin, apparently from its heating system, and they were told to come down low and open the hatch.

"At first we thought the fumes would disperse and they could go on. But they said they felt so ill they couldn't continue," Noble said, so the decision was taken to abort the flight. He said the touchdown at sea was "very smooth", but the two could not be lifted clear by helicopter because the gondola was partly covered by the balloon.
